The modifications in `fnic_fcs.c` are primarily focused on reducing log spamming by controlling when the port speed is printed, ensuring it only occurs during driver initialization or when there is a change in speed. This change is directly related to the previous implementation that printed the port speed every 2 seconds, which was deemed excessive. 

The modification in `fnic_trace.c` complements the changes in `fnic_fcs.c` by ensuring that the log message regarding the firmware reported port speed is correctly phrased, thereby improving the clarity and accuracy of the logs generated by the driver. Together, these changes enhance the logging behavior of the driver while also fixing a minor typographical error.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
shost_printk(KERN_INFO, fnic->lport->host, "Current vnic speed set to :  %llu\n",
			(u64)atomic64_read(
			&fnic->fnic_stats.misc_stats.current_port_speed));
```
Reason:
The above code statement logs the current port speed to syslog every time the `fnic_handle_link` function is called, which occurs every 2 seconds. This results in excessive log entries and spamming, as it does not check whether the port speed has changed before logging.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (old_port_speed != new_port_speed)
	shost_printk(KERN_INFO, fnic->lport->host,
				"Current vnic speed set to :  %llu\n",
				new_port_speed);
```
Reason:
The added conditional check ensures that the port speed is only logged if it has changed from the previous value (`old_port_speed`). This prevents redundant log entries and reduces log spamming, as the speed will only be printed during driver initialization or when a change in speed occurs.
